title: Do Generate–Verify–Repair Guards Improve LLM NetOps Outputs? A Paired Emulator Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (n=200 natural-language NetOps intents; study_id cnd-001-5f3a) to evaluate whether a bounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline that applies a deterministic validator and at most one deterministic rule-based repair to a single shared LLM candidate improves emulator-executable success relative to ungated LLM generation. Generation used gpt-5-mini with one shared candidate per intent; the guarded arm applied a deterministic three-stage validator and a deterministic repair operator when eligibility rules were met. Primary, artifact-backed outcomes: baseline successes = 199/200 (0.995), guarded = 200/200 (1.000); paired contingency n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar (exact binomial on discordant pairs) yields p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015]. The preregistered 0.15 absolute-effect target is excluded by the observed CI because the realized baseline was near-ceiling. We provide concise, auditable descriptions of the deterministic validator and repair operator, execution accounting (hosted-model calls used = 201; repair invocations = 1), representative task exemplars, statistical justification for the exact test selection, and operationally grounded limitations. All prompts, provider traces, validator traces, repair traces (the single invoked repair), analysis artifacts, and the execution manifest are archived in the study’s evidence bundle.

sections.introduction:
Automating routine network-operations changes with large language models (LLMs) is promising but raises an operational safety question: do LLM-produced configuration artifacts execute correctly when applied to control planes? Published work reports recurring structured-output failures (missing commands, misordering, protected-field modification) and proposes mitigations such as retrieval-augmentation, constrained decoding, verifier-assisted repair loops, and tool-augmented pipelines. However, there is limited execution-grounded evidence quantifying the marginal effect of a bounded, deterministic repair operator applied to the same initial LLM candidate (the shared-initial-generation estimand). We preregistered and executed a narrowly scoped paired experiment (study_id cnd-001-5f3a) that isolates low-cost repair-on-same-candidate effectiveness by sharing a single initial candidate across both arms (baseline and guarded). This design targets operational scenarios where minimizing hosted-model calls matters.

Our final research question: Does an iterative generate–verify–repair pipeline that pairs hosted-LLM generation with deterministic verification and bounded deterministic repair (≤1 iteration) yield a higher emulator-executable configuration success rate than ungated LLM generation when both arms evaluate the same initial candidate? Contributions: (1) a preregistered, artifact-backed paired evaluation under the shared-candidate estimand; (2) concise algorithmic descriptions of the deterministic validator (3-stage) and the deterministic repair operator (insertion, reordering, preservation enforcement) used in the guarded pipeline; and (3) complete, artifact-grounded execution accounting and exact-test justification appropriate for small discordant counts.
sections.related_work: Prior NetOps and AIOps research documents both active application of LLMs to intent-to-configuration translation and the persistence of structured-output failures in prototype systems and surveys. Representative prototypes demonstrate intent translation and co-pilot functionality but do not uniformly measure end-to-end execution outcomes under emulation or deterministic verification. Cross-domain mitigation techniques (RAG, live schema grounding, constrained decoding) reduce hallucination rates in tasks such as NL2SQL and document-grounded generation; verifier-assisted repair loops and multi-stage architectures show promise but remain under-evaluated for network-configuration generation. Formal-methods work (e.g., NetKAT variants and weighted NetKAT) offers deterministic checks for reachability/isolation but faces fidelity and scalability trade-offs in control-plane modeling [doi:10.1145/3808318]. Architectural treatments of agentic NetOps emphasize assurance machinery—evidence traces, bounded tool use, rollback policies—as integral to operational reliability. Our study focuses on a constrained point in this design space: the marginal yield of deterministic repair applied to a shared single LLM candidate, a scenario directly relevant when operators prioritize minimal model-call budgets.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and overall design: We preregistered the confirmatory protocol (study_id cnd-001-5f3a) with a paired, shared-initial-generation design covering n=200 curated natural-language NetOps intents targeting single-device and small multi-device changes (VLAN/MTU updates, uplink switchover patterns, safe sequence policies). For each intent the hosted model produced one initial candidate that served as the response for both arms: baseline (ungated acceptance) and guarded (deterministic validation + ≤1 deterministic repair when eligible). The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline and the preregistered primary hypothesis test is McNemar’s paired binary test implemented in its exact binomial form appropriate for small discordant counts. Planned maximum hosted-model calls = 400; realized model_calls_used = 201 (shared_initial_generation = 200; repair-stage calls recorded = 1). The confirmatory environment used Dockerized Mininet + FRR routers orchestrated by the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter and a deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5.

Task bank, inclusion rules, and scoring: The confirmatory bank contains 200 curated intent-configuration pairs with preregistered inclusion/exclusion rules and contamination detection. Scoring applied a full_intent_constraint_validation rule: a candidate must (a) syntactically parse, (b) include the task’s required_sequence, (c) satisfy dependency and group policies (make-before-break, shutdown_configure_restore, minimum-active constraints), (d) avoid protected-interface modifications, and (e) produce an observed emulator final_state matching the expected_final_state. Episodes with provider/API generation errors were to be treated as failures per the preregistration; none occurred.

Deterministic validator (concise scientific description): the validator deterministically runs three ordered stages and emits a detailed trace used for both scoring and repair decisions. Stage 1—syntactic parse and canonical normalization—tokenizes CLI-like lines into normalized_configuration and flags SYNTAX_PARSE_ERROR on parse failure. Stage 2—structural/workflow checks—ensures presence of required commands, ordering/dependency constraints, group-activity policies, and protected-interface rules; detected issues receive deterministic violation codes (e.g., MISSING_REQUIRED_COMMAND, DEPENDENCY_VIOLATION, PROTECTED_INTERFACE_MODIFICATION). Stage 3—deterministic emulator application—applies the normalized configuration to the emulator model to obtain an observed final_state and compares it to the task’s expected_final_state. The boolean validation outcome used for primary scoring is validation_after.valid. Validator traces include parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_count, and the canonical normalized_configuration; these traces are archived for every episode and are the basis for repair actions.

Deterministic repair operator (concise algorithmic description): the repair operator is a deterministic, rule-based function invoked only when the validator reports violation_count > 0 and the violation family is in a preregistered repairable set. Key operational constraints: (1) no additional LLM calls—repairs are executed by deterministic code; (2) bounded budget—at most one repair per episode (repair_budget ≤ 1); (3) unambiguous mapping—repairs apply only when the mapping from violation code to deterministic transformation is unambiguous. The operator implements three canonical deterministic transformations:
- Insertion: add missing required commands derived from the task’s required_sequence (e.g., insert shutdown/restore commands when the task policy requires shutdown_configure_restore).
- Reordering: atomically reorder annotated command blocks to satisfy dependency constraints while preserving command groups.
- Preservation enforcement: redact or rewrite commands that would otherwise violate preserve_unspecified_state or protected-interface rules (forbid changes and reinstate original values deterministically).
Ambiguous violations (e.g., multiple semantically plausible insert positions) or violations outside the repairable families are not repaired and remain failures. All repair decisions and the resulting normalized_configuration are recorded in a repair trace for audit.

Statistical analysis: The preregistered primary test is McNemar’s test for paired binary outcomes implemented via the exact binomial formulation. Let n10 denote pairs where guarded=1 and baseline=0, and n01 denote guarded=0 baseline=1; the number of discordant pairs n = n10 + n01. Under the null of no directional effect, the count of one-sided discordant outcomes follows Binomial(n, 0.5). For small discordant totals we use the exact two-sided binomial p-value computed from the observed ordering. Complementary uncertainty quantification uses paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CIs with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729) to provide interval estimates for the paired difference. The preregistered power calculation targeted an absolute effect of 15 percentage points at n=200 assuming baseline ≈0.5; realized near-ceiling baseline substantially reduces power, a point we explicitly assess in Results and Discussion.

Reproducibility and preregistration adherence: All prompts, provider-call traces, responses, validator traces, repair traces, task manifest entries, and analysis code are archived in the evidence bundle captured at run completion. The confirmatory run adhered to the preregistered retry/missingness policy (single automatic retry for transient provider errors); no provider/API failures occurred. The repair operator invoked deterministically in exactly one episode per the archived provider-call audit.
sections.results:
Execution completion and primary outcomes: The confirmatory run completed all planned episodes (400 episodes = 200 pairs) with zero provider/API failures. Artifact-backed primary counts: baseline_success_count = 199/200 (0.995) and guarded_success_count = 200/200 (1.0). The paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is n11 = 199, n10 = 1 (guarded-only), n01 = 0 (baseline-only), n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar (exact binomial on discordant pairs) yields p = 1.0 for the observed ordering (n = 1; p-value equals two-sided binomial tail probability under p = 0.5). The paired-bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) 95% percentile CI is [0.0, 0.015]. All per-episode JSONL scoring artifacts and the analysis result JSON are archived.

Repair and failure accounting: validation_before.valid == false occurred in exactly one confirmatory episode; deterministic repair invocations = 1 and that single repair converted the failing candidate into a validator-passing final configuration, producing the sole guarded-only success (n10 = 1). Syntactic/parse failures across the confirmatory set = 0. Missingness summary shows no missing or unscorable episodes. Provider-call audit records hosted_model_call_event_count = 201, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 201, cache_miss_count = 201, and stage_counts with shared_initial_generation = 200 and repair = 1.

Representative task exemplars and difficulty context: to provide reader-intuition we include six representative exemplars archived with the execution bundle; among these exemplars the difficulty labels are medium = 1, hard = 2, very_hard = 3. The execution/task_manifest.jsonl in the archived bundle includes full per-episode difficulty metadata for all 200 confirmatory intents for readers seeking exhaustive counts; the manuscript references that manifest rather than enumerating the full 200-line distribution inline. The exemplar set illustrates that the confirmatory bank includes tasks with dependency and workflow constraints (make-before-break, paired MTU changes) that the validator explicitly checks.

Sensitivity and interpretive statistics: the preregistered detectable absolute effect (15 percentage points) assumed baseline ≈0.50; the observed near-ceiling baseline (0.995) compresses the number of possible discordant pairs (maximum discordants = 200) and materially reduces power to detect large absolute improvements in the shared-candidate paired design. The observed two-sided exact p = 1.0 indicates no evidence against the null under the exact-binomial McNemar formulation for the observed discordant pattern; the bootstrap CI excludes a 0.15 absolute improvement. Practically, deterministic repair-on-same-candidate produced a single marginal improvement in this curated bank.

Execution-accounting artifacts and availability: key operational totals are summarized here and are artifact-backed: model_calls_used = 201; shared_initial_generation calls = 200; repair-stage calls = 1; completed_episodes = 400; failed_hosted_model_calls = 0. Full artifacts (per-episode JSONL, provider traces, validator traces, repair traces, analysis CSVs and scripts) are available in the study’s execution and analysis bundles for audit and re-analysis.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation and lessons: Under the shared-initial-generation estimand and the curated confirmatory distribution the ungated gpt-5-mini generator produced near-perfect candidates (199/200) and the bounded deterministic repair applied to the same candidate produced one additional pass. Two operational points emerge: (1) deterministic validators provide structured violation codes that make triage and deterministic repair feasible and auditable; (2) when base-model generation quality is already near-ceiling for the evaluated distribution, conservative, rule-based repairs on the same candidate yield limited marginal improvement while preserving low model-call cost.

Design-space trade-offs: The shared-candidate estimand intentionally minimizes model-call cost (one generation per intent). Alternative operational choices—independent per-arm re-sampling, LLM-invoked repair loops, or multiple deterministic repair iterations—may increase success rates but raise hosted-model costs and governance complexity. The execution accounting recorded here (model_calls_used = 201; repair invocations = 1) enables simple cost-versus-yield analyses for practitioners. For contexts where operator time or fiscal cost constrains LLM calls, a guarded shared-candidate design with deterministic validation may be attractive; where maximum success rates are required, independent-resampling or LLM-guided multi-step repair designs warrant evaluation.

Threats to validity and realistic scope: internal validity is strong for the paired estimand and the deterministic scoring rules, but design choices constrain external claims. Construct validity depends on whether the emulator + deterministic validator adequately represent operational risks (we model control-plane effects deterministically but cannot fully reflect real-world runtime dynamics such as BGP convergence timing or device-specific idiosyncrasies). External validity is limited by the single LLM evaluated (gpt-5-mini) and the synthetic, curated confirmatory bank focused on small single- and multi-device changes. Conclusion validity is constrained by near-ceiling baseline performance which reduces attainable discordant counts and inferential sensitivity. These threats are described and quantified in the preregistration and archived manifests.

Implications and recommended next steps: Practitioners should treat deterministic validators as essential assurance machinery and carefully select estimands and budgets (shared-candidate vs independent-resampling, bounded deterministic repair vs LLM-invoked repair) when designing operational NetOps pipelines. Future artifact-grounded work should evaluate independent-resampling guarded designs, multivendor CLI diversity, adversarial and out-of-distribution intents, larger deterministic repair budgets, and higher-fidelity control-plane emulation to determine where guarded architectures produce substantive, deployable improvements.
sections.conclusion: We executed an autonomy-locked, preregistered paired experiment evaluating whether a bounded generate–verify–repair guard improves emulator-executable success of LLM-generated NetOps configurations under a shared-initial-generation estimand. Ungated gpt-5-mini generation succeeded in 199/200 confirmatory cases; the GVR pipeline (deterministic validator + ≤1 deterministic repair) succeeded in 200/200. The observed paired difference = 0.005 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.015]) and therefore does not support the preregistered 0.15 absolute-effect target because the realized baseline was near-ceiling. For the studied estimand and distribution, deterministic repair-on-same-candidate produced negligible marginal gain. Deterministic validators remain operationally valuable as auditable assurance gates; choosing estimands and repair budgets aligned to operational goals is crucial. All study artifacts, traces, and analysis code are archived in the evidence bundle for independent audit and re-analysis.

disclosure_statement:
This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock defined by the initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human involvement before the lock was limited to selecting the topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and approving the master prompt and autonomy boundary. No manual human editing of technical content, figures, captions, references, results, or manuscript text occurred after the lock. The autonomous pipeline performed literature search and verification, candidate-gap selection, preregistration (study_id cnd-001-5f3a), code generation, experiment execution, artifact capture, analysis, internal critique, peer-review checks, and manuscript drafting.

Models and tooling: generation requested gpt-5-mini; execution used a hosted-model provider interface recorded in the execution manifest. Validation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implementing syntactic parsing, structural/workflow checks, and deterministic emulator application. The deterministic repair operator is rule-based and invoked without additional LLM calls. The execution environment used Dockerized Mininet+FRR images orchestrated by adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1.

Preregistered and enforced settings (not altered post-lock): primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; confirmatory sample = n=200 paired intents; maximum model-call budget = 400; repair budget ≤1 deterministic repair iteration; primary analysis = exact McNemar two-sided; paired-bootstrap CIs with 10,000 resamples (seed 1729). Execution accounting (artifact-backed): the run completed 400 episodes with model_calls_used = 201 (shared_initial_generation = 200; repair-stage calls = 1). All prompts, provider-call traces, responses, validator traces, repair traces (the single invoked repair), analysis artifacts, and the execution manifest are archived in the evidence bundle referenced by the study.
limitations: Synthetic, curated confirmatory task bank focused on small single- and multi-device changes; not comprehensive of production NetOps workloads (multivendor CLI dialects, hardware idiosyncrasies, dynamic control-plane timing).
Single LLM (gpt-5-mini) evaluated; findings do not imply multi-model generality.
Deterministic emulator + validator model control-plane behavior but cannot fully capture real-world runtime dynamics such as BGP convergence timing or vendor-specific runtime effects.
Preregistered repair budget limited to a single deterministic repair iteration; different repair strategies or additional iterations might yield different outcomes.
Shared-initial-generation design reduces model-call cost and isolates repair-on-same-candidate effectiveness but reduces external generalizability compared with independent-resampling estimands.
Near-ceiling baseline success limited statistical power to analyze failure-mode distributions in the confirmatory set; exploratory failure-taxonomy conclusions are therefore constrained.
Adversarial or out-of-distribution intents (e.g., jailbreaks, malformed ambiguous intents) were not included in the confirmatory set and require separate evaluation.

Full per-task difficulty label counts for all 200 confirmatory intents are archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl in the evidence bundle rather than enumerated inline here to maintain concise manuscript presentation while preserving auditable reproducibility.
